# SCL for a tester

> **Reader:** tester. **Already knows:** how to verify behaviour and what evidence looks like. **Next step:** understand, then verify the model is met. **Human-constraint budget:** ~14 min read · cognitive load **M**.

The model is the source of truth. This narrative is generated from it.

## Judgements a person owns

Validation cannot certify these. A human owns the judgement.

- `outcome-backwards-compatibility` ⚖ A person decides whether older projects still work, where that is practical.
- `outcome-context-survives` ⚖ A new person can reconstruct the reasons from the project alone.
- `outcome-ai-outcome-aligned` ⚖ A person can tell whether the generated work still serves the outcome.
- `outcome-ai-understanding-inspectable` ⚖ You can read what the assistant assumed before any build starts.
- `outcome-reviewers-understand-min-constraint` ⚖ The write-up is as short as it can be without hiding a risk the reader owns.
- `outcome-uncertainty-visible` ⚖ Open risks stay on a single list, and a recommendation that depends on one says so.
- `outcome-prerequisites-verified` ⚖ Work stops when a critical skill is missing, and says what to restore.
- `outcome-constraints-reliable-not-restrictive` ⚖ Rules block real violations and still allow a new approach that follows the rules.
- `outcome-verification-role-aligned` ⚖ The project checks the right scope and does not keep a second, drifting copy of the truth.

## Releases are consistent and reproducible

Outcomes: `outcome-consistent-frameworks`, `outcome-reproducible-releases`.

The interaction that turns tagged source into a consumable release.

- `requirement-versioned` (delivery, implemented). Acceptance: Given a release folder named v0.1.0, when its manifest is read, then version is 0.1.0. — Every release carries a version that matches its folder name.
- `requirement-change-docs` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a release folder, when it is checked, then RELEASE.md and CHANGELOG.md exist. — Every release explains what changed.
- `requirement-reproducible` (delivery, implemented). Acceptance: Given a release, when its kit is compared with that release's source snapshot, then every file matches and the digest matches. — Each release kit matches the source snapshot recorded for that release.
- `requirement-self-contained` (architectural, implemented). Acceptance: Given the release folder, when its text files are scanned, then none contain a network URL, an absolute home path, or a link that leaves the folder. — A release folder copied on its own does not point outside itself.

## Upgrades are predictable

Outcomes: `outcome-predictable-upgrades`, `outcome-backwards-compatibility` ⚖.

The interaction in which a maintainer publishes how to move off the previous release.

- `requirement-upgrade-instructions` (delivery, implemented). Acceptance: Given a second release folder v0.2.0 after v0.1.0, when it is checked, then UPGRADE_FROM_v0.1.0.md exists. The first release does not need one. — Every release after the first explains how to move off the previous one.

## A release only when consumers are affected

Outcomes: `outcome-predictable-upgrades`, `outcome-releases-mean-consumer-impact`.

The interaction that decides whether a change set is allowed to become a release.

- `requirement-release-eligibility` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a change set of only meta/ and changelog/ paths, when eligibility is classified, then the result is no release. Given a change under src/schemas/, the result is release. — A release is cut only when a project-consumable asset changed. Internal-only edits are recorded as framework work, not a release.
- `requirement-consumer-impact-test` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a release, when RELEASE.md is read, then Consumer impact is YES and a behavioural difference of at least 20 characters is recorded. NO is a failed release. The release change list must include a consumer asset. — Before a release, answer whether a project on the previous release would behave differently. NO prohibits the release. There is no first-release exception.

## The model captures why

Outcomes: `outcome-intent-visible`, `outcome-context-survives` ⚖, `outcome-ai-outcome-aligned` ⚖.

- `requirement-capture-why` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given the model, when validate runs, then there is at least 1 Intent and 1 Outcome, and every Requirement reaches an Intent. — The model records why the work exists, not only the rules, and every rule traces back to that why.
- `requirement-context-persistent-inspectable` (non-functional, implemented). Acceptance: Given every evidence pointer, when it is opened, then the file is inside the repository and the anchor is present. — A new person or a new session can reconstruct the contextual network from the repository alone.
- `requirement-raise-gap-challenge` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a gap challenge, when it is formatted, then it contains POTENTIAL MODEL GAP and the four labels, and it writes no model file. — A suspected missing interaction becomes a challenge with an observation, a concern, possibilities, and a question. - `requirement-model-holds-test-preconditions` (governance, planned). Acceptance: Given a future test record, when it is derived, then its precondition, trigger, and expected result already exist on the model. Not enforced in 0.1.0. — Preconditions, the trigger, and the expected result live in the model before any test is written.

## Required skills are verified first

Outcomes: `outcome-prerequisites-verified` ⚖.

The interaction that discovers skills, verifies them, and only then runs a significant operation.

- `requirement-skills-registry` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given meta/required-skills.md, when it is parsed, then every skill has those five fields and a known criticality. — meta/required-skills.md lists each skill with five fields: id, name, purpose, criticality, and verification.
- `requirement-verify-skills-before-ops` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a registry whose critical skill file is missing, when validate runs, then it exits with a FAIL report and does not continue. — The harness discovers skills, verifies them, and only then runs the operation. A missing critical skill stops the run and names the skill, the impact, and the action.

## Constraints bound solutions without restricting them

Outcomes: `outcome-constraints-reliable-not-restrictive` ⚖.

The interaction that executes within layer roles and fails a solution only on a real boundary violation.

Model status: partial.
Known gap: The boundary check is implemented. There is no full execution runtime, and the vector threshold in OQ-001 is unresolved.

- `requirement-interpreter-honours-layers` (functional, implemented). Acceptance: Given the layer-role contract, when a solution is assessed, then only requirement boundaries can fail it. — Intent dominates, outcomes are what you optimise, models are the logical shape, and requirements are hard boundaries. The engine's private method is not prescribed.
- `requirement-no-expressiveness-penalty` (governance, implemented). Acceptance: Given a solution whose only novelty is an unknown field, when it is assessed against a boundary on a different field, then it passes. Given the forbidden value, it fails. — Only a real boundary violation may fail a solution. Failing a new approach that still follows the rules is a defect.
